text: An exporter ships goods today, then waits ninety days to get paid. Hisab on Monad pays them now, in dollars.

One click loads the invoice. A shipping bill for forty-eight thousand seven hundred fifty A U S D, and a credit tier. Tier one: eighty percent advance, twelve and a half percent A P R. So the offer is thirty-nine thousand.
Across the board, a lender picks an amount, mints test dollars, and deposits. They get pool shares, and the pool gets cash to lend.
The buyer acknowledges the invoice with one signature over the amount and the due date. No signature, no financing.

Now the exporter accepts. The receivable locks into the pool, and thirty-nine thousand lands in their wallet. One transaction, confirmed in about one point two seconds. That's Monad's fast blocks and tiny fees.
Try to finance the same invoice twice? Already locked. The contract just says no.
When the buyer pays, one transaction splits the money. The pool is repaid first, principal plus seventy-five days of interest. A small fee. And the rest goes to the exporter.
Paid on time, so the credit history improves. Tier two: eighty-eight percent advance, at a lower rate. The next invoice is offered at forty-two thousand nine hundred.
And the lender? Their share price ticks up. Real yield, from real trade.
Every step lands on the explorer. Registered, acknowledged, financed, paid, each one with its own transaction link.
That's Hisab on Monad. Try it live at hisab dash monad dot vercel dot app.
